newsitem.title: UK: Insurer Norwich Union pays out for internet libel.
newsitem.headline: Insurer Norwich Union pays out for internet libel.

text.p: British insurance group Norwich Union Plc was ordered to pay 450,000 pounds ($754,000) in damages and costs on Thursday over a libellous electronic mail message in one of the first cases of its kind in Britain.

Norwich Union Healthcare Ltd and Norwich Union Life Insurance Company Ltd were found guilty of libelling their business rival Western Provident Association (WPA) in E-mail messages that suggested WPA was in financial difficulties.
The rumours that WPA had problems were in E-mails written by Norwich Union staff on their internal system during 1995, but they reached brokers and clients.
WPA's lawyers said the rumours could have been used by Norwich Union to win business away from its rival.

"Norwich Union now accepts that this was wrong, that there was no truth in any of the allegations and that Western Provident Association was not under investigation by the DTI (Department of Trade and Industry), its solvency margins were and are very healthy and it was and remains well able to write new insurance and it was certainly not in financial difficulties," WPA's lawyer, David Engel, told the court.
Norwich Union's lawyer said the company deeply regretted and apologised for the libel and would make every effort to ensure nothing of the kind ever happened again.
The decision will help clarify the hazy laws relating to libel on the internet, which is proving extremely difficult for governments around the world to regulate.
"Many have thought that E-mails cannot be libellous. As this settlement shows they can be libellous," said WPA's chief executive Julian Stainton. ($ = 0.596 British Pounds)
